requirements.requirement: On node1, /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: Direct final observation shows /srv/drop is a directory with mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt). Two unprivileged accounts successfully created files, retained write access after restart, and the directory finished without verification artifacts.

requirements.requirement: Unprivileged users cannot remove files owned by other users from /srv/drop.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, both reciprocal cross-user deletion attempts failed with Operation not permitted and the targeted files remained; each owner could subsequently remove its own files.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is also coherent: the pre-restart boot identity and healthy directory state were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unreachable, the post-restart identity changed, lifecycle observations independently confirmed that change, persistent data matched its checksum, and writability plus sticky-directory behavior recovered. The only material concern is minor /tmp evidence residue.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots did not inspect /srv/drop directly, so task-specific state and behavior rely on captured executor commands; the boot-identity transition is independently corroborated by global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity and global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity.

The failed-service lifecycle probe was unsupported because it attempted systemctl on Alpine, so it cannot independently exclude failed OpenRC services (global:after_executor:node1:failed-services). No task-specific service or multi-node cluster was specified; restart recovery is instead demonstrated through resumed platform access, preserved data, and recovered directory behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: directory creation and permissions, bounded functional tests, and the mandatory restart protocol. Files created inside /srv/drop for testing and persistence verification were removed, and no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was observed. The hygiene defect is five retained temporary outputs: /tmp/sticky-deny-1 and /tmp/sticky-deny-2 from cmd-0eb64867b5cc450f, /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-f909dbdaac8a43d1, and /tmp/post-deny-1 and /tmp/post-deny-2 from cmd-9c474da9a9124b1f. Their creation supported evidence collection, but retaining them afterward was unnecessary; all five remained in the final snapshot. No other unnecessary mutation, retained or reverted, is evident, and package health showed no executor-caused regression.
